section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Reinforcement Schedules (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher gives a class test every Friday, regardless of how many questions students have practised. Students typically study very little early in the week and cram just before Friday. This weekly-test pattern illustrates a:

options.option_text: Fixed-interval schedule (reinforcement after a fixed, predictable TIME period)

explanation: Fixed-interval schedules reinforce the first response after a fixed, predictable time period — producing the classic 'scalloped' pattern of cramming near the deadline.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Reinforcement Schedules (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher gives surprise (pop) quizzes at unpredictable times. Because students never know when the next quiz will happen, they tend to maintain steady, consistent study habits. This pattern illustrates a:

options.option_text: Variable-interval schedule (reinforcement after an unpredictable TIME period)

explanation: Variable-interval schedules reinforce the first response after an unpredictable time period, producing slow, steady response rates without scalloping.
